title: Custom Bevel Gears - UAlberta FSAE
summary: Engineered a custom 1:1 bevel gear transmission using parametric CAD modelling, gear geometry calculations, and assembly validation for CNC manufacturing.
description: Engineered a custom 1:1 bevel gear transmission using parametric CAD modelling, gear geometry calculations, and assembly validation for CNC manufacturing.
objectives: Redesign the steering gearbox to replace the existing unequal-ratio bevel gears with a compact 1:1 transmission, improving steering predictability and driver feedback without modifying the original shafts or housing.
contributions: Engineered a custom bevel gear pair from first principles, deriving tooth geometry parametrically in SolidWorks rather than relying on standard off-the-shelf gear models.
Evaluated the existing 16- and 24-tooth configurations and developed a matching 20-tooth design to balance tooth strength, packaging constraints, and undercut risk.
Created and validated the complete gear assembly, resolving geometric constraints and preparing manufacturing-ready CAD models for CNC machining by a team sponsor.

process.title: Reverse Engineering & Design Constraints
process.body: Analyzed the existing steering gearbox to identify the geometric constraints imposed by its shaft locations, mounting interfaces, and housing. The original unequal gear sizes were replaced with a symmetric 20:20 tooth configuration, achieving the desired 1:1 ratio while preserving the 45° shaft intersection.

process.title: Parametric Gear Geometry
process.body: Derived the gear geometry using standard bevel-gear equations. The 45° shaft angle and equal tooth counts established pitch-cone angles of 22.5° for both gears. Constructed the tooth profiles around a 20° pressure angle, using equations to control the geometry and maintain dimensional consistency as parameters changed.

process.title: Tooth Taper & Profile Development
process.body: Unlike spur gears, bevel gear teeth decrease in size toward the cone apex. Used pitch-cone relationships to determine the required variation in tooth-space geometry, incorporating a 1.5° draft between the large and small ends. This required accounting for the three-dimensional tooth shape rather than simply extruding a constant cross-section.

process.title: Assembly Validation & Manufacturing Handoff
process.body: Positioned the gears using shaft-axis mates and applied mechanical gear constraints in SolidWorks to verify the 1:1 rotational relationship. Reviewed the gear placement and clearances within the original gearbox envelope, then finalized the CAD geometry for CNC machining. This provided an opportunity to translate theoretical gear calculations into a manufacturable mechanical design.

results: Delivered a complete parametric CAD model of a custom bevel gear set, with geometry defined by engineering calculations and tailored to the existing steering assembly.
Established a 1:1 transmission across a 45° shaft angle using matching 20-tooth gears with 22.5° pitch-cone angles.
Completed digital assembly and kinematic validation, then submitted the finalized designs to a team sponsor for CNC manufacturing.
lessons: The most challenging aspect was translating idealized bevel-gear equations into a three-dimensional tooth profile that could fit within an existing mechanical assembly. The project demonstrated how shaft geometry, tooth count, pressure angle, and taper must be considered together rather than independently.

It also reinforced the importance of parametric modelling when working with tightly constrained designs. Linking dimensions to mathematical relationships made the geometry easier to refine and reduced the risk of inconsistencies between revisions.

The next stage is physical validation of the machined gears, particularly backlash, tooth contact patterns, and steering response under load. These measurements will help determine whether the theoretical geometry translates into the intended mechanical performance.
